children: GLP Japan has raised 600 billion yen ($3.76 billion) to create a fund for building logistics centers in the country, capitalising on an influx of overseas capital, the Nikkei newspaper reported on Tuesday.
GLP Japan is the Japanese subsidiary of Singapore-based logistics company GLP.
Investments by the Tokyo-based GLP Japan's fund, including borrowing, will total 1.7 trillion yen, establishing it as the country's largest real estate fund, Nikkei said.
Investors hail primarily from outside Japan, the report said. That includes the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, which allocated 150 billion yen.

The funds raised will allow for the construction of 30 to 40 large facilities in Tokyo, Nagoya and Osaka. Alongside cold-storage warehouses, there will be facilities equipped for e-commerce, the report said.
GLP could not be immediately reached for a Reuters request for comment outside normal business hours.
Government-backed and pension funds from Asia, the Middle East, the U.S. and Europe, as well as Japanese institutional investors, will also provide backing, Nikkei reported.
